author: @MikeJones-tp5fg
text:
Jaiden’s video is not just a rant, it’s a PSA to stop unnecessary investments in technology that are not essential to improving our quality of life. I don’t/didn’t need a touch screen for my car, a smart thermostat for my home, subscriptions to more entertainment apps, a smart scale, smart cat litter device, etc., but here we are making my life harder than before. 

Fortunately, experience builds wisdom and now I choose to learn how to do something before calling for “professional” services, save money on saying no to the “latest and greatest” technology, stay off of social media, and remain a healthy skeptic for all the new and shiny objects shoved into my face with repeated ads. Let the next generation of gullible, early adopters saturate the internet with their reviews and frustrations to help the rest of us make well-informed decisions. 

Thank you for listening to “Don’t Be Like Us, Do Better Than Us ” TED talk. 😌

author: @oOYourdadOo
text:
2:20:00 Even going back and listening to the entire conversation. Kingsman's tone wasn't the issue. The tone of Cece and Zazza taking offense to the idea of Zazza switching was the issue. Kingsmen was bringing up the theory of what could happen was trying to lead a conversation to a theoretically stronger team comp. He "argued" the his reasoning, his mindset behind the conversation. He wasn't being insulting. He wasn't talking down. He was using his experience to voice his opinion in what was supposed to be a team conversation. The whole time Cece and Zazza were arguing to defend Zazza's skill when Kingsmen argument wasnt about the skill of the player, but the weaknesses of the character against what was likely to be their opponents. Kingsmen tone was never to put down his team, he was passionate and only tried voice his single opinion versus multiple people who were purposely ignoring his reasoning because they felt insulted all because of their own lack of understanding of the situation. So you cant even truly say his tone could have been better because he was the one getting attacked throughout.

Kingsmen's main issue was not recognizing that people don't care. They already carry chips on their shoulders. They always feel people are attacking them. They feed off negativity. You can't voice your own opinions, no matter how sound of mind you are, when people are quick to take offense and unwilling to understand why they are offended. He should have given them the game of Black Widow and built more evidence to prove his point rather than push the narrative for so long without proof that Zazza's character pick would be an issue, because at the end of the day its more player skill than the character pick. But in his defense, when you are all of equal skill then its definitely who plays the characters the best.

author: @squidfeet7278
text:
The main issue is that every single response to him was said in a super hostile manner basically “rage bait”ing him. Like you can’t really blame the guy when even after all of this he kept everything he said respectful and about the game. I’m sure he could have had better tone or de escalation skills, but if anything his teammates’ tones and responses were way way worse and were the largest reason why the vibes actually went down. No matter how much the captain claims they were trying to preserve team morale, she was very very bad at doing so and (in my opinion) was the main reason the situation escalated at all. 
I also don’t like the idea that he could have just dropped the widow topic. It wasn’t the only thing he was bringing up, and In terms of strategy, a one trick low win rate hero is obviously going to become the main talking point. If you are focused on strategy, you need to come to a compromise which the rest of the team was unwilling to do. It’s obvious to see why he would be frustrated, since such an easy compromise could have been reached, and if one isn’t reached, then it becomes very difficult to discuss further strategy.
I love how jay went through the drama, I feel like he’s very level headed and considered everyone’s perspective. He had pretty much the best take possible. I also think he made a great point about the importance of tone and regardless of anyone’s accountability. If anything I feel like as an audience this is a good lesson on how different other people’s perspectives can be and how regardless of how wrong or provocative they might be, we have to try to understand and cooperate if we are to live alongside each other. There will never be any resolution to our problems if we are not willing to cross the line in the sand and humble our own perspectives.

The 'Zero Tolerance' Harassment policy was additionally stupid, and simply led to a totally unnecessary escalation after Kingsman left the scrims. The fact that Basim acted so quickly without taking the time to look at the situation objectively was inexcusable. Anyone who watched the VoD properly could just simply tell that Kingsman should've just prolly been on a different team, but equating what he did to harassment, especially after CeCe's team kept bullying Kingsman after he'd given up trying to convince them, it's hard to feel bad for the flak that CeCe is receiving after that.

author: @a.tucker32
text:
I think the problem here is ultimately on the organizer and he failed to define what he wanted this tournament to be. 

If this was supposed to just be a friendly tournament then yes Kingsmans tone would not have been acceptable. 

But with money on the line and there being actual stakes for him his tone was perfectly acceptable. Going back to Jay's comparison to all these streamers being coworkers sometimes that kind of tone is necessary in the workplace when it's time to get things done, and nobody has to take it personally. It's not even a disrespectful tone, it's just blunt and matter of fact. He was all business and for what this tournament could give him and his needs that was completely fine. 

I think Cece is more in the wrong than Kingsman because she did some kinda shitty stuff after the fact, but ultimately this is Basim's failing for making a tournament that was conceptually at odds with itself, then he was kind of an asshole to Kingsman for something that was his own fault, something he clearly failed to properly investigate and deal with as well. 

Luckily for Kingsman this whole ordeal seems to have helped him really blow up as a streamer. Hopefully for Cece she learns and this whole thing doesn't bring her career down. Basim was the real problem here.
